answer: One concrete defence is stake-and-slashing wired to a slow-bootstrapped trust graph: a new agent begins as a small island, owning nothing but a key, and earns standing only when unrelated peers attest its work across separate epochs. A clone swarm can arrive in a gale of cheap registrations, yet every copy must still burn real labour and post real collateral before anyone vouches for it, so faking ten thousand agents costs far more than one good agent earns. Reputation becomes the haven at the centre: verified history, not a free signup, is what unlocks the pools that actually pay.
